title: Sender address and the way to the SMTP server
interface:
namespace Drupal\hwdesk\Service; final class MailTransport (declare(strict_types=1)). New file.
Everything the mail plugin needs to know before it sends: which address the mail comes from, which server to hand it to, and how to describe a failure so that a human can act on it without the password ending up in the log.
Constructor: __construct(\Drupal\Core\Config\ConfigFactoryInterface $configFactory, ?\Drupal\key\KeyRepositoryInterface $keyRepository = NULL). Registered in hwdesk.services.yml as 'hwdesk.mail_transport' with arguments ['@config.factory', '@?key.repository'] (already written; do not touch). The key repository is optional on purpose: the module declares key:key as a dependency, so a real site always has it, but a kernel test that does not enable the Key module must still be able to build the container.
Read config 'hwdesk.settings' on every call (the tests change it at runtime): mail_from, mail_from_name, mail_reply_to, smtp_enabled (bool), smtp_host, smtp_port (int), smtp_security ('none'|'tls'|'ssl'), smtp_user, smtp_key (the id of a Key entity, never the password itself).
The password is read only through $this->keyRepository->getKey($id)?->getKeyValue(); a missing key or an empty id means no password, which is not an error. When the repository itself is NULL (the Key module is switched off) and trim(smtp_key) is not '', there is likewise no password, and keyMissing(): bool must return TRUE so that the caller can log a reason instead of sending unauthenticated mail into a void. keyMissing() is FALSE in every other case, including an empty smtp_key.
Public methods:
- isSmtp(): bool -- TRUE only when smtp_enabled is truthy AND trim(smtp_host) is not ''. A switched-on SMTP without a server address is not SMTP; otherwise the mail would quietly disappear.
- dsn(): string -- the Symfony mailer DSN. Not SMTP -> exactly 'sendmail://default'. SMTP -> scheme 'smtps://' when smtp_security is 'ssl', otherwise 'smtp://'; then, when trim(smtp_user) is not '', rawurlencode(user), and when a password was found ':' . rawurlencode(password), then '@'; then the trimmed host, ':' and the port; finally '?auto_tls=false' when smtp_security is 'none' (so an administrator who asked for an unencrypted connection gets one instead of a silent STARTTLS). Both scheme names and the auto_tls option are what symfony/mailer understands (vendor/symfony/mailer/Transport/Smtp/EsmtpTransportFactory.php). Never build the DSN with string interpolation of an unencoded user name: an at sign in 'asistentka@firma.cz' would break the address.
- from(): array -- ['address' => mail_from, 'name' => mail_from_name] when trim(mail_from) is not '', otherwise an empty array [] (then the site default stands). The name may be ''.
- replyTo(): string -- trim(mail_reply_to), possibly ''.
- describeFailure(\Throwable $e, string $where): string -- one line for the log that says the reason, the place in the application and the place in the code: the exception's getMessage(), the $where the caller passed (for example 'odeslani protokolu'), and basename($e->getFile()) . ':' . $e->getLine(). Before returning, remove the password: when it is not '', replace every occurrence of it AND of rawurlencode(password) in the whole line with '***'. Symfony puts the complete DSN into its connection errors, so without this the password lands in the log the moment the server is unreachable.
No logger (the caller logs), no \Drupal:: static calls, no echo or print, nothing else public.

uses.Mail settings form (the exact config key: web/modules/hwdesk/src/Form/MailSettingsForm.php: the form that writes the keys named above

database: not applicable (config and the Key module only)
forbidden: Reading the password from config, from settings.php or from an environment variable: it lives in a Key entity, nowhere else.
Returning a DSN with an unencoded user name or password.
Letting the password, or its url-encoded form, stay in the text describeFailure() returns.
Writing hwdesk.services.yml, the form or the test.
